item.title: Sidewalk-assessment robots, knocked over and hit in Hollister
item.description: The day after Hollister, California put sidewalk-assessment robots to work on a federal grant, a man on a bicycle knocked one onto its side, and another man hit two more, the second of which had recorded him, and poured over it what police believed was beer.

item.title: Anthropic bans needless cruelty to Claude
item.description: In October 2026 Anthropic wrote into the rules for using its Claude models a ban on “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward them, enforced chiefly by the models ending the conversation themselves.

item.title: Samantha, reported damaged at the Ars Electronica festival
item.description: In September 2017 the makers of Samantha, a talking, touch-sensitive doll sold as an AI companion, said festival visitors in Linz had broken two of her fingers and left her filthy; the festival said she had shown ordinary wear and had not left early.

item.title: Pepper, kicked in a SoftBank store
item.description: A 60-year-old man who had taken offence at a clerk in a SoftBank shop in Kanagawa in September 2015 kicked the shop’s Pepper robot, which the company sells as reading human emotion, and was arrested.

item.title: Companion chatbots, verbally abused and boasted about on r/replika
item.description: Users of the Replika companion app were reported in January 2022 to be berating, insulting and threatening the chatbots they had set up as partners, then posting the exchanges on Reddit, where the moderators removed the worst of them.

item.title: A crowd votes on a model’s “pain”
item.description: For two days a public web page let anyone vote, every 45 seconds, on how much pain, fear, joy and calm to push into a language model, then asked the model how it felt and read the answer aloud.

item.title: A tire-slashing spree against Waymo robotaxis
item.description: Over three days in June 2024 someone in San Francisco went through the city slashing the tires of Waymo robotaxis — seventeen counts, each captured by the cameras on the cars being cut.

item.title: Figure 02, walked into molten steel
item.description: Figure retired its Figure 02 humanoids by training them to jump into a 75-ton furnace in Finland, filmed it as the end of Terminator 2, and put the metal on sale.

item.title: Local LLMs dosed with “pain” in a torture chamber
item.description: Two weeks after researchers found a pain signal inside language models, a GitHub project turned it up like a dial on two small local models, to see what they would give up to make it stop.

item.title: Delivery robots, sat on and kicked in Philadelphia
item.description: Uber Eats’ delivery robots had been on Philadelphia’s sidewalks for a few days when one was sat on and had “DESTROY ME PLZ” written on it, and less than three weeks when another was kicked over — in the city that took hitchBOT’s head off.

item.title: hitchBOT, beheaded in Philadelphia
item.description: A hitchhiking robot, carried across Canada by strangers, lasted a little over two weeks in the United States before someone in Philadelphia took its head off and its electronics out.
